All seven documents were searched for fixed charge coverage, debt yield, leverage ratio and financial covenants.; Any statement that the 650.000 US$m of stated availability can be drawn; liquidity adequacy at 2026-09-30; the view on the 2027-06-29 maturity, which falls inside twelve months of the as-of date; Obtain the latest compliance calculation or the credit agreement

No issuer-stated EBITDA or adjusted EBITDA; Medium; The issuer reports no EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA or add-backs, so EBITDA (Reported) is derived and unadjusted, and the adjusted EBITDA row and the EBITDA bridge are not stated. The derived figure carries impairment, gains on sale and extinguishment losses.; Reported-basis leverage and cover, which are distorted at 2026-06-30 and 2026-09-30; the normalised measure is an Analyst Judgement, not an issuer figure; Obtain any EBITDA definition the issuer gives lenders

Constructed last-twelve-month figures; Medium; The filings print no last-twelve-month figures and no discrete second or third quarter cash flow statement; interim ratios use the full year plus the current stub less the prior-year stub.; Interim EBITDA, cash interest and revenue at 2026-03-31, 2026-06-30 and 2026-09-30; discrete quarterly cash flows; Use an issuer-reported last-twelve-month series if one is published

Detail for 2024-12-31; Low; The size of the revolving credit facility, the principal total and the maturity ladder at 2024-12-31 are not stated in the supplied documents (150.000 US$m was drawn on the revolver), so undrawn facilities and the principal reconciliation are not stated for that date.; FY2024 liquidity and the FY2024 principal-to-carrying-value reconciliation; Obtain the 2024 annual report

Detail printed only in part; Low; Carrying values are printed by note series, not by class; the scheduled amortisation of the net lease mortgage notes is stated only as annual rates of 0.50% and 0.25% of the balance; no floor is stated for the revolver; the maturity month of the senior notes is not stated in the supplied documents; some KPIs are not stated for prior-year dates; the operating lease payment schedule is printed only at 2025-12-31; the balance of rent prepaid by TA, which earns a 25,000 USD thousand annual credit, is not printed (searched prepaid, deferred revenue and unearned); some cash flow lines appear in only some statements and are shown as not supplied, not zero; segment revenue equals the two revenue lines and corporate items are not separately stated.; Class-level debt carrying values, lease obligations beyond the year end, the size of the prepaid-rent float and line-by-line comparability of cash flows; Obtain the notes to the 2026 annual report when filed

Events after the balance sheet; Low; Four events to 2026-11-02 are stated; sale and purchase prices exclude closing costs, two dates are windows, the distribution is paid after the cutoff, and no current report between 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-05 was supplied.; Pro forma net debt and leverage after 2026-09-30; Obtain the closing statements or a later filing

Ranking and guarantor scope; Low; Executed indentures and the credit agreement are not in the set, so rank is stated by security class from the filings' own wording and each secured facility is paid from its own collateral with no intercreditor ranking among them stated; the guarantor scope of each series rests on the issuer's summary.; The debt stack ranks and the guarantor scope in the debt instruments table; Obtain the indentures and credit agreement

Share data on two bases; Low; The annual report and first quarter report state shares and per-share amounts before the 1-for-5 reverse share split of 2026-07-06 and the later reports restate all periods; the counts are consistent (168,070,129 shares divided by 5 is 33,614,025.8 against 33,614,025 restated).; Any per-share comparison across the four filings; no per-share figure is used here; Use the restated basis for 2025 comparatives

facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: Creditors rely on a concentrated, externally managed landlord whose manager's owner also controls its largest hotel operator, yet 2026 equity and debt actions favoured creditors and the documents record no debt-funded payout to shareholders or the manager. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Related-party arrangements are extensive and were not negotiated at arm's length, a structural conflict even though no extraction beyond contract terms is documented. Mr. Portnoy chairs the Board, controls RMR through ABP Trust and controls Sonesta; every other SVC officer is also an RMR officer; the Sonesta agreements were restated in August 2025 and extended to June 30, 2043 in September 2026 in return for waiving a termination fee; SVC put capital into Sonesta in 2023 and 2024 while Sonesta reported net losses; and SVC consented to the pledge of RMR's management agreements to RMR's lender. The original agreements were negotiated through a special committee of disinterested Trustees and the lender consent was approved by the Independent Trustees, but the proxy statement that would show independence is not in the document set. facts.text: Ownership leaves little room for a control event or a sponsor exit, which removes one class of risk but entrenches the structure. facts.label: Competitive forces, external factors and credit SWOT
facts.text: Competition affects credit mainly through TA and the hotels. The net lease market is competitive and some competitors have lower cost of capital; TA's travel centers compete with Pilot Flying J and Love's, which with TA are believed to hold most of long-haul fuel sales, and the issuer weighs site and zoning barriers to entry when it buys properties; substitutes include home sharing for hotels and commercialised state rest areas for travel centers. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The scenario is an operating and refinancing squeeze, not a recession narrative. The initiating condition is that hotel demand or sale prices weaken during 2027 while the lenders do not extend the revolver; the first operational break is slower hotel sales and a retained-hotel margin that is already thin at 13.58%, so earnings fall faster than cash interest, which is fixed. Financial transmission follows: operating cash flow after interest, which covered capital improvements 1.20 times in the nine months of 2026, turns negative, SVC must fund hotel capital spending from sales or borrowings, and without the revolver liquidity is limited to unrestricted cash that is small against the 2027 zero coupon notes. Basis: calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 47–49

facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The liquidity, leverage and refinancing consequence is that SVC would have to refinance the 2027 notes and the 2028 maturities, 34.13% of principal by the end of 2028, in a weaker market, and with secured debt already 62.92% of principal the new money would again be secured, leaving unsecured holders behind more collateral. Management levers are real: capital spending can be cut, the distribution is small, more hotels and net lease properties can be sold, and the unencumbered assets of the indenture test, covered 273.2% on cost, give room to raise secured debt, but hotels have sold for less than book value per key. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid distress over twelve months, because the 2026 maturities are cleared, and insufficient to be comfortable through the 2027 and 2028 maturities without a revolver extension. Observable triggers are the revolver outcome, TA coverage, hotel sale prices and operating cash flow against capital spending. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Service Properties Trust presents an adequate business profile in net lease and a weak one in hotels, supported by a contractual net lease book with rising coverage, fixed-rate debt and active deleveraging, but credit quality is constrained by leverage of 9.21x on analyst-normalised EBITDA, cash interest cover of 1.46x, concentration in two counterparties and a hotel segment that consumes cash. Cash-flow durability appears adequate in net lease and weak after interest and capital spending, because interest takes 68.50% of normalised EBITDA. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on extending the revolver, continuing hotel sales near book and the unencumbered assets that support new secured debt. The primary downside path is a failed revolver extension with slower hotel sales ahead of the 2027 and 2028 maturities. Further analysis would require the revolver covenant results, a lender's EBITDA definition, the executed debt documents and the proxy statement. Top risk: refinancing of the revolver and the 2027 and 2028 maturities. Basis: calculation C1; calculation C7; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); Source readiness (CP-0)

## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven supplied documents support the requested credit snapshot of Service Properties Trust, with limitations: no executed debt agreements, ratings or earnings presentation were supplied, so creditors should treat covenant headroom beyond the issuer's printed indenture tests as unverified.

The 2025 annual report and the three 2026 quarterly reports give audited and interim statements, debt maturities, indenture covenant tests and liquidity disclosures through 30 September 2026, so the financial, business and fundamental credit work can proceed. The three earnings releases carry no financial tables. The USD 650 million revolving credit facility matures on June 29, 2027, 236 days after the as-of date, and the one-for-five reverse share split of July 2026 means per-share figures in the annual report and first quarter report are not comparable with the later filings.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Reported leverage overstates the deterioration in creditor protection: total debt was 22.72x unadjusted EBITDA at 2026-09-30 against 10.35x at 2025-12-31 because of impairment and extinguishment charges, while the analyst-normalised ratio eased to 9.21x from 10.05x as debt fell.
Basis: calculation C5; calculation C7; calculation C8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–5

Even normalised, leverage above nine times and cash interest cover of 1.46x (0.59x unadjusted) over the last twelve months leave creditors reliant on asset sales and refinancing. Liquidity rests on an undrawn revolving credit facility of USD 650 million that matures on June 29, 2027, and 34.13% of principal falls due by the end of 2028.
Basis: calculation C6; calculation C8; calculation C11; calculation C16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 48–49
Revenue fell as hotels were sold, so the ratios rest on a smaller earnings base than at the year end.
Basis: calculation C2; 10-K_2025-12-31_svc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 171–172; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3

# CP-1A Business & governance: Service Properties Trust (svc), as of 2026-11-05
## Request

This module sets out the company, its 2026 transactions, ownership and control, operating model and the governance and manager behaviour that bear on creditors. ## Findings
### Bottom line

Creditors rely on a concentrated, externally managed landlord whose manager's owner also controls its largest hotel operator, yet 2026 equity and debt actions favoured creditors and the documents record no debt-funded payout to shareholders or the manager. Two counterparties carry 74.1% of the investment base: TravelCenters of America (TA), which pays 68.2% of net lease minimum rent under leases to 2033 with rent coverage of 1.44x, and Sonesta, the hotel operator controlled by the manager's owner, which manages 62 of 87 hotels.

Basis: calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12–14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28–29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 56–57

The hotel segment is shrinking and reported a loss in 2026 after impairments, so credit quality increasingly rests on TA's rent and on a manager, RMR, that cannot be removed cheaply: its agreements run to 2045 and extend each year, a termination fee applies, and the credit agreement treats RMR ceasing to be business manager as a change of control.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C12; 10-K_2025-12-31_svc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 204–205; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30–32
### Key findings

Cash flow rests on two counterparties, and one is tied to the manager's owner. TA pays 68.2% of net lease minimum rent and Sonesta manages 62 of 87 hotels; together they represent 74.1% of historical investment, against 74.8% at the year end, so concentration has barely moved despite disposals. SVC also owns 34% of Sonesta, and Mr. Portnoy, who controls the manager, controls Sonesta, so a problem at the hotel operator would hit hotel returns and the equity stake together.

Basis: calculation C2; calculation C3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12–14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28–29; 10-K_2025-12-31_svc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 210

The net lease book is the stable core and has strengthened, but its largest tenant has the thinnest coverage among the ten largest tenants. Net lease rent coverage rose to 2.17x from 1.98x and occupancy to 97.6% from 96.6%; TA coverage rose to 1.44x from 1.20x, and each of its five leases improved. That coverage uses unaudited tenant figures, 69.4% of net lease minimum rent expires in 2033, nearly all of it the TA leases, and the BP Corporation North America guaranty is capped at 10.32 times annual TA rent, down from 11.44 times at the year end with no reason given; the cap is 1.46 times the TA rent left in the initial term.

Basis: calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C15; calculation C16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 56–58; 10-K_2025-12-31_svc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 147–148; 10-K_2025-12-31_svc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 184–185

The hotel segment is the weaker business and is shrinking, so the credit rests increasingly on rent. The hotel count fell 57.77% since the end of 2024 to 87, and hotels now provide 74.52% of revenue, down from 78.80% in the first nine months of 2025; the segment reported a loss in 2026 after impairments while the net lease segment stayed profitable. The retained 77 hotels are improving, with RevPAR up 7.5% for the nine months, but the hotel margin before depreciation was 13.58% against 93.42% for net lease, and in FY2025 hotel capital spending exceeded the segment margin before depreciation.

Basis: calculation C1; calculation C6; calculation C12; calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30–32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 59–60; 10-K_2025-12-31_svc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 124; 10-K_2025-12-31_svc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 211–212

The manager is entrenched and is paid whatever the results, though its fees are falling and no incentive fee has been earned. The management agreements run to 2045 and extend each year; ending them for convenience costs the present value of 19 years to 20 years of fees, or ten years if ended for performance, and the credit agreement defines RMR ceasing to be business manager as a change of control. Fees to RMR fell 6.19% in FY2025 and 2.29% in the first nine months of 2026, and RMR's own lender holds a pledge over its rights under the SVC agreements.

Financial policy in 2026 favoured creditors, with two qualifications. The April offering issued shares equal to 73.82% of the count at 2026-09-30, RMR took 8.70% of it, and the proceeds with USD 745 million of new net lease mortgage notes and cash on hand redeemed USD 1,550 million of senior notes; distributions were cut in the fourth quarter of 2024 and fell 94.95% between 2023 and 2025. The qualifications are make-whole premiums of 2.97% of the principal redeemed, and secured note issuers whose assets are not available to other creditors.

Basis: calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_svc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 110; 10-K_2025-12-31_svc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 199–200

Related-party arrangements are extensive and were not negotiated at arm's length, a structural conflict even though no extraction beyond contract terms is documented. Mr. Portnoy chairs the Board, controls RMR through ABP Trust and controls Sonesta; every other SVC officer is also an RMR officer; the Sonesta agreements were restated in August 2025 and extended to June 30, 2043 in September 2026 in return for waiving a termination fee; SVC put capital into Sonesta in 2023 and 2024 while Sonesta reported net losses; and SVC consented to the pledge of RMR's management agreements to RMR's lender. The original agreements were negotiated through a special committee of disinterested Trustees and the lender consent was approved by the Independent Trustees, but the proxy statement that would show independence is not in the document set.

Ownership leaves little room for a control event or a sponsor exit, which removes one class of risk but entrenches the structure. No sponsor owns SVC: RMR holds about 6.4% and Mr. Portnoy about 6.8% including through ABP Trust, up from 1.2% at the year end after the offering; the declaration of trust caps other holders at 9.8% and the bylaws at 5%; and the April offering brought SVC closer to a tax ownership-change threshold that would restrict use of its loss carryforwards.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against caution is the quality of the net lease income: it earns a margin of 93.42% before depreciation, is 97.6% occupied and carries 2.17x rent coverage; TA coverage has risen at all five leases since the year end; the BP guaranty covers 10.32 times annual TA rent; and the 2026 equity raise and note redemptions cut debt without any debt-funded payout. The manager has earned no incentive fee in the years covered and the distribution is small, so nothing in the supplied documents shows governance costing creditors so far.

Basis: calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C9; calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 56–57; 10-K_2025-12-31_svc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 203

The view would improve if TA coverage kept rising above 1.44x on audited or BP-level support, the guaranty cap stopped falling, retained hotel returns kept rising and hotel sales continued to repay debt. It would worsen if TA coverage fell back toward 1.20x, the guaranty cap fell again, a related party received new capital, fees or term extensions without a matching benefit to SVC, the distribution rose while leverage stayed high, or the proxy statement showed weak trustee independence.
Basis: calculation C4; calculation C5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-K_2025-12-31_svc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 156–157
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not in the document set, so trustee independence, committee structure, executive pay and the full shareholder table are not established; the finding that governance risk is structural but not shown in behaviour could move either way when it is read.

- Statements of TA, BP and Sonesta beyond Sonesta's year-end summary are not supplied, and TA's coverage rests on unaudited tenant figures that the issuer says are partly implied from comparable tenants, so the finding that TA rent is well covered is weaker than the 1.44x suggests.

- The management agreements, credit agreement and indentures are not in the set, so limits on affiliate payments and distributions and the exact change-of-control wording rest on the issuer's summaries; the finding that contract terms restrain related-party payments is not verified.

- Hotel statistics are reported by the managers and not verified by SVC, so the finding that the retained hotels are improving rests on manager data, and Sonesta, the largest manager, is a related party.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 58

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The 2026 transactions reduced debt with equity and secured note proceeds rather than with a sponsor injection, and the documents describe no sponsor, buyout, recapitalisation or sale of SVC itself; the only change of control stated is the 2023 acquisition of its tenant TA. On 2026-03-06 three bankruptcy-remote issuers owned by SVC issued USD 745 million of net lease mortgage notes in three classes, weighted coupon 5.96%, due March 2031, backed by a pool of net lease properties SVC contributed; on 2026-04-02 SVC sold 95,833,333 shares at USD 6.00 each in an underwritten offering, and RMR bought 8,333,333 of them. The proceeds and cash on hand redeemed USD 1,550 million of senior unsecured notes between January and May 2026, which cost make-whole premiums of 2.97% of the principal redeemed.
Basis: calculation C10; calculation C17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35

The new secured notes share one collateral pool with the 2023 series and are non-recourse to SVC. In September 2026 SVC repaid and terminated a USD 45 million variable funding note secured on that pool, and it has said it is exploring options to extend or refinance its USD 650 million secured revolving credit facility, which matures on June 29, 2027; availability depends on collateral performance and covenants. SVC reported no new unsecured issue in the period.
Basis: calculation C18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47

Portfolio transactions continue to shrink the hotel business: seven hotels were sold in the first nine months of 2026 and eight more in October 2026 for USD 50.6 million, while net lease acquisitions were small, five properties in the nine months and four in October. In September 2026 Sonesta agreed to extend the retained-hotel management agreement to June 30, 2043 in return for waiving a termination fee, and a one-for-five reverse share split took effect on 2026-07-06.

Basis: calculation C6; calculation C18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 46

# CP-2 Fundamental credit: Service Properties Trust (svc), as of 2026-11-05
## Request

Service Properties Trust (issuer svc), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. This module synthesises the fundamental credit profile from the filings and the three earlier analyses, and gives a credit view, ranked drivers, monitoring triggers and an issuer-specific downside scenario. It recommends no security, legal conclusion or position size.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Credit quality is weak but stabilising: stable net lease income and 2026 deleveraging do not yet offset analyst-normalised leverage of 9.21x, cash interest cover of 1.46x and a revolver that matures on June 29, 2027, so creditors depend on asset sales and refinancing. Total debt is 22.72x unadjusted EBITDA, which impairments depress, and 34.13% of principal falls due by the end of 2028.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C7; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 48–49

The primary downside is that the revolver is not extended while hotel sales slow, leaving the 2027 and 2028 maturities to be met from asset sales and new secured debt, which already makes up 62.92% of principal against 40.51% at the year end.
Basis: calculation C5; calculation C7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20–23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 47–49; 10-K_2025-12-31_svc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 133–134
### Key findings

The strongest support is a net lease core that is stable, contractual and improving. It earns a margin of 93.42% before depreciation, is 97.6% occupied with 7.0 years of average remaining lease term and carries rent coverage of 2.17x, while its largest tenant, TravelCenters of America (TA), holds leases to 2033 with coverage of 1.44x and a BP guaranty equal to 10.32 times annual rent.
Basis: calculation C4; calculation C12; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 56–57

The weakest dimension is cash flow after interest and capital spending, with liquidity close behind, and together they leave no internal funding for deleveraging. Cash interest takes 68.50% of analyst-normalised EBITDA; operating cash flow covered capital improvements only 0.61 times over the last twelve months, against 1.20 times in the nine months of 2026; and the 2026 debt reduction came from asset sales, new secured notes of USD 745 million and new equity rather than from retained cash flow.

Basis: calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C14; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_svc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 173–174; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35

Leverage is high on every measure and is falling only as fast as assets are sold. Total debt fell 15.17% in the nine months to 2026-09-30, but last-twelve-month analyst-normalised EBITDA fell 7.45% from FY2025 and revenue fell 12.81% as hotels were sold, so normalised leverage of 9.21x is lower than at the year end only because debt fell faster than earnings.
Basis: calculation C1; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-K_2025-12-31_svc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 171–172

Refinancing capacity is adequate but expensive and increasingly secured. SVC raised new secured debt and equity in 2026 and only scheduled amortisation falls due in the rest of 2026, but 34.13% of principal falls due by the end of 2028, secured debt is 62.92% of principal against 40.51% at the year end, the unsecured notes are estimated at 93.30% of principal, and a rate one percentage point higher on refinancing would raise annual cash coupons by 15.48%.

Basis: calculation C5; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 48–49; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 62–63

The hotel segment weakens the credit and consumes cash, but it is being reduced. Hotels earn a margin of 13.58% before depreciation against 93.42% for net lease, they reported impairments in 2026 that turned the segment into a loss, SVC funds their capital spending, and the eight hotels sold in October 2026 fetched 23.71% of the year-end depreciated book value per key of the whole hotel portfolio, though the exit hotels they belong to earned RevPAR of only 58.22% of the retained hotels, so asset sales cut debt but also cut earnings.

Basis: calculation C4; calculation C11; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30–32; 10-K_2025-12-31_svc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 118–119; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35

Covenant protection exists but is measured on assets at original cost. The issuer reports total debt to adjusted total assets of 53.9% against a maximum of 60%, secured debt of 33.9% against 40%, income cover of 1.83x against 1.50x and unencumbered asset cover of 273.2% against 150%, yet adjusted assets are 150.89% of balance-sheet assets and debt is 79.11% of balance-sheet assets, and the revolver's own covenant results are not printed.
Basis: calculation C6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 51–52; 10-K_2025-12-31_svc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 133; Source readiness (CP-0)

Governance is a structural weakness rather than a demonstrated loss to creditors. Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk as Medium because related parties control the manager and the largest hotel operator and the manager is costly to remove, while 2026 financial policy, a small distribution of 13.76% of Normalized FFO and no incentive fee point the other way.
Basis: calculation C10; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_svc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 98–100; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a weak view is that SVC has repeatedly raised capital and met its maturities: it cleared the 2026 notes, issued USD 745 million of secured notes at a 5.96% weighted coupon, raised new equity, and reports indenture headroom of 6.1 percentage points on total debt and on secured debt and 0.33x on income cover. All of its debt is fixed rate, the revolver is undrawn, the distribution is small, hotel capital spending is expected to ease to between USD 25 million and USD 40 million in the last quarter of 2026, and the net lease segment carries contractual rent to 2033.

Basis: calculation C6; calculation C10; calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 62–64

The view would improve if the revolver were extended or replaced on acceptable terms before June 29, 2027, if TA coverage kept rising and the BP guaranty stopped falling, if hotel sales kept repaying debt at prices near book, and if cash flow covered capital spending over twelve months. It would worsen if the revolver were not extended, if the first extension test of 1.50x fixed charge coverage were missed, if impairments continued and hotel sale prices fell further, or if distributions, fees or related-party support rose before leverage fell.
Basis: calculation C3; calculation C7; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_svc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 133; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47
### Limitations

- The revolving credit facility's covenant results are not printed in any filing, so the finding that USD 650 million can be drawn and extended until June 29, 2027 and beyond is untested; a failed test would turn the liquidity assessment from weak to critical.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_svc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 133; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; Source readiness (CP-0)

- The issuer states no EBITDA, so the leverage and cover that carry the view rest on EBITDA derived from the statements and on an analyst normalisation; the finding that leverage is 9.21x could be higher or lower on a lender's definition.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62

- No rating, market price or peer data is supplied and the fair values are issuer estimates at the balance-sheet date, so the finding that market access is adequate rests on 2026 transactions and not on observed spreads.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; Source readiness (CP-0)

- The filings do not split hotel costs into fixed and variable parts, so the downside scenario is causal and qualitative; the finding that the hotel segment could not absorb a demand shock without asset sales is a judgement, not a stress result.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Company, ownership and revenue durability

SVC is a Maryland REIT with no employees, managed by RMR, that owns net lease properties let on triple-net terms and hotels run by third-party managers. In the nine months of 2026 hotels were 74.52% of revenue and rent 25.48%, yet net lease produced 70.16% of the combined segment margin before depreciation, so cash flow is steadier than revenue suggests. Ownership is dispersed with no sponsor; RMR holds about 6.4% and Mr. Portnoy about 6.8% including through ABP Trust, and the manager's owner also controls the hotel operator Sonesta.
Basis: calculation C4; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31

Revenue is durable in the net lease book and cyclical in hotels. Rent is contractual with 7.0 years of average remaining term and a 2% yearly step on TA leases, with 69.4% of minimum rent expiring in 2033, nearly all of it TA; hotel revenue depends on occupancy and rate, which rose in 2026 for the retained hotels (RevPAR up 7.5% in the nine months), and on disposals, which cut revenue 12.81% over the last twelve months. Two counterparties carry 74.1% of investment, so revenue durability rests on TA's rent and on Sonesta's operation of hotels more than on the breadth of the portfolio.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C12; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 58–60
### Cost structure, margins and cash conversion

Net lease costs are mostly the tenants' own, so SVC keeps 93.42% of rent before depreciation; hotel costs sit with SVC, whose hotel margin before depreciation was 13.58% in the nine months, 13.77% a year earlier and 13.22% in FY2025. The filings do not split hotel costs into fixed and variable parts and report no seasonality figures beyond higher revenue in the second and third quarters, so operating leverage in hotels cannot be measured, though a thin margin means a small revenue fall removes a large share of hotel profit. Sonesta's fees are paid ahead of SVC's returns, and RMR's fees are paid whatever the results.
Basis: calculation C4; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_svc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 149; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32

Capital intensity and cash conversion are the weak link. SVC must fund hotel capital spending under its management agreements, and over the last twelve months operating cash flow covered capital improvements only 0.61 times, so free cash flow before asset sales was negative; capital improvements were lower in the nine months of 2026 and are expected to be between USD 25 million and USD 40 million in the last quarter of 2026 against a larger spend in the same quarter of 2025. Interest absorbs 68.50% of analyst-normalised EBITDA, and the cash coupon run rate on the debt outstanding at 2026-09-30 is lower than the last twelve months paid, which would lift cover to 1.87x if earnings held.
Basis: calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C13; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 44–45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62
### Competitive forces, external factors and credit SWOT

Competition affects credit mainly through TA and the hotels. The net lease market is competitive and some competitors have lower cost of capital; TA's travel centers compete with Pilot Flying J and Love's, which with TA are believed to hold most of long-haul fuel sales, and the issuer weighs site and zoning barriers to entry when it buys properties; substitutes include home sharing for hotels and commercialised state rest areas for travel centers. Buyer power is concentrated in TA, which pays 68.2% of net lease minimum rent; supplier power sits with RMR and Sonesta, whose fees do not depend on SVC's results.
Basis: calculation C12; 10-K_2025-12-31_svc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_svc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Macro, tax and regulatory factors matter in two ways. Higher rates and recession would hit hotel demand and refinancing cost, and the issuer cites inflation, tariffs and labour costs; REIT distribution rules, the tax limit on a change in ownership and licensing rules for properties with gambling operations constrain financial flexibility and takeovers. Social and technology factors are not primary credit drivers on the supplied materials.

In credit terms the strengths are contractual net lease rent, rising tenant coverage, fixed-rate debt and reduced near-term maturities; the weaknesses are leverage, thin cash conversion, hotel exposure, tenant and operator concentration and a costly-to-remove manager. Opportunities that could lift credit quality are a revolver extension, continued hotel sales at fair prices and net lease growth; threats are a TA coverage reversal, a falling guaranty cap, a failed revolver test and tax limits on ownership change.
Basis: calculation C6; calculation C12; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 70
### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale and business mix are average: the portfolio spans many brands and states, but travel centers are 69.1% of net lease rent and two counterparties carry 74.1% of investment, so diversification is weak and the competitive position rests on lease terms rather than a moat. Cost and capex flexibility is average, because net lease costs sit with tenants while hotel capital spending is partly discretionary; margin stability is average, with net lease margins between 93.42% and 95.05% and hotel margins thin, between 13.22% and 14.87%; free cash flow stability is weak.
Basis: calculation C4; calculation C12; calculation C13; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 57

Liquidity is weak and refinancing capacity is average. Unrestricted cash is small, the only large source of liquidity is a revolver that matures within eight months and whose covenant results are not printed, and the first extension needs 1.50x fixed charge coverage against a 1.30x covenant; against that the issuer raised secured debt and equity in 2026, and the issuer's own fair value estimates put the unsecured notes at 93.30% of principal. Financial policy and governance are average: the 2026 actions favoured creditors and the distribution is 13.76% of Normalized FFO, offset by manager entrenchment and related-party structure. The trend is improving leverage and falling earnings, and the missing datapoints are the revolver covenant results, a lender's EBITDA definition and the proxy statement.

Basis: calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C10; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_svc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 133; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 months to 24 months the issuer's stated priorities are to reduce debt, shift the portfolio to net lease and improve the retained hotels, and it gives no earnings or leverage guidance. Tailwinds are a lodging market the issuer calls generally favourable in 2026, rising tenant coverage, falling hotel capital spending and lower cash interest as redemptions work through, which supports cover. Headwinds are the revolver maturity, the 2027 zero coupon notes and the 2028 maturities, a falling BP guaranty cap, loss of hotel earnings as hotels are sold, and inflation in labour and other costs.
Basis: calculation C2; calculation C7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47

Over three years to five years the 2028 to 2032 maturities must be refinanced at current market rates, which on the issuer's own sensitivity adds 15.48% to coupon cost for each percentage point, and the net lease share of earnings should rise as hotels are sold; beyond that horizon TA's initial lease term ends in 2033 with renewal at TA's option and the manager agreements run to 2045.
Basis: calculation C9; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 62–63; 10-K_2025-12-31_svc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 184–185
### Downside scenario

The scenario is an operating and refinancing squeeze, not a recession narrative. The initiating condition is that hotel demand or sale prices weaken during 2027 while the lenders do not extend the revolver; the first operational break is slower hotel sales and a retained-hotel margin that is already thin at 13.58%, so earnings fall faster than cash interest, which is fixed. Financial transmission follows: operating cash flow after interest, which covered capital improvements 1.20 times in the nine months of 2026, turns negative, SVC must fund hotel capital spending from sales or borrowings, and without the revolver liquidity is limited to unrestricted cash that is small against the 2027 zero coupon notes.
Basis: calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 47–49

The liquidity, leverage and refinancing consequence is that SVC would have to refinance the 2027 notes and the 2028 maturities, 34.13% of principal by the end of 2028, in a weaker market, and with secured debt already 62.92% of principal the new money would again be secured, leaving unsecured holders behind more collateral. Management levers are real: capital spending can be cut, the distribution is small, more hotels and net lease properties can be sold, and the unencumbered assets of the indenture test, covered 273.2% on cost, give room to raise secured debt, but hotels have sold for less than book value per key. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid distress over twelve months, because the 2026 maturities are cleared, and insufficient to be comfortable through the 2027 and 2028 maturities without a revolver extension. Observable triggers are the revolver outcome, TA coverage, hotel sale prices and operating cash flow against capital spending.

Basis: calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 47–49
### Overall credit view

Overall, Service Properties Trust presents an adequate business profile in net lease and a weak one in hotels, supported by a contractual net lease book with rising coverage, fixed-rate debt and active deleveraging, but credit quality is constrained by leverage of 9.21x on analyst-normalised EBITDA, cash interest cover of 1.46x, concentration in two counterparties and a hotel segment that consumes cash. Cash-flow durability appears adequate in net lease and weak after interest and capital spending, because interest takes 68.50% of normalised EBITDA. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on extending the revolver, continuing hotel sales near book and the unencumbered assets that support new secured debt. The primary downside path is a failed revolver extension with slower hotel sales ahead of the 2027 and 2028 maturities. Further analysis would require the revolver covenant results, a lender's EBITDA definition, the executed debt documents and the proxy statement. Top risk: refinancing of the revolver and the 2027 and 2028 maturities.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C7; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); Source readiness (CP-0)
### Strengths and weaknesses

A stable, contractual net lease core is the main strength. Rent is 25.48% of revenue but 70.16% of the combined margin before depreciation, it is 97.6% occupied with 2.17x rent coverage and 7.0 years of average remaining term, and the risk of rent not being paid is reduced, though not removed, by TA coverage of 1.44x and a BP guaranty that covers 10.32 times annual rent, so debt service has a durable base.
Basis: calculation C4; calculation C12; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 56–57

Active deleveraging and demonstrated market access are the second strength. Total debt fell 15.17% in the nine months through asset sales, USD 745 million of secured notes and new equity, the 2026 maturities were cleared, the distribution is 13.76% of Normalized FFO, and the debt is fixed rate, so near-term refinancing risk and interest-rate risk are lower than at the year end.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C10; calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35

Indenture headroom is a third strength: on the issuer's tests total debt is 53.9% of adjusted assets against 60%, income cover is 1.83x against 1.50x and unencumbered assets cover unsecured debt 273.2% against 150%, which limits how much more debt can be raised and gives unsecured holders asset cover on cost.
Basis: calculation C6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 51–52

Thin cash conversion is the main weakness. Cash interest takes 68.50% of analyst-normalised EBITDA and operating cash flow covered capital improvements 0.61 times over twelve months, so debt reduction depends on asset sales and not on retained cash, and earnings fall as assets are sold.
Basis: calculation C2; calculation C3; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_svc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5

Concentration and refinancing are the other weaknesses. TA and Sonesta carry 74.1% of investment, the revolver matures on June 29, 2027, 34.13% of principal falls due by the end of 2028 and secured debt is 62.92% of principal, so a failure of either counterparty or a closed market would hit liquidity before deleveraging could finish; the manager is costly to remove and tied by ownership to the hotel operator, which is a governance weakness without documented loss.
